scientific_conditions.evidence: All actual source tasks concern refraction/index/TIR or lens definitions/formula/rays/magnification. No reflection or mirror-motion task was imported from a warning or parent claim.
The refraction answer uses n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r), valid at i = r = 0. It neither treats the 0/0 sine quotient as an index nor asserts a unique plane when incident ray and normal coincide.
n1 > n2, normal reference, r = 90 degrees at equality and TIR strictly above critical angle are preserved identically.

Actual and backward-extension foci are distinguished. Signed formula handles real/virtual objects/images without asserting every converging image is real or every diverging image virtual. F = -10,d = -5 yields a real f = +10.

Construction C is conditional on an actual ray through the left focus. For a real object inside F, that focal point lies on the supporting line behind the source, not on the actual source-to-lens segment. The statement does not promise otherwise; this inside-focus supporting-line application and full construction are not assessed.

ZHEN_checks.evidence: Both preserve ordinary isotropic media, fixed frequency, normal-measured angles, existing transmission and the same general product-law options.
Both define c/v phase-speed roles and n21 as medium 2 relative to medium 1; every ratio/order is identical.
Both preserve n1 > n2 > 0, normal reference, finite incidence range, strict below/above comparisons, equality and inverse functions.
Both compare axial separation to the same curvature, conjugate, diameter or wavelength scales and retain identical universal/approximate qualifiers.
Both distinguish actual outgoing convergence from backward-extension incident-side virtual focus and preserve each center/finite-image distractor.
Both preserve finite nonzero signed distances, real/virtual convention, positive unknown coefficient and the prospective versus actual-emitter distinction.
Both restrict to a converging lens and left-to-right light; 'through the left principal focus' and 'always' center-to-focus distractor retain the same segment reading and quantifier.
Both define object H > 0 and image h >= 0 as size magnitudes; image/object, unsigned versus signed, and linear versus squared ratios match.

package_review.dependency_note: Focus question A and construction question A share a standard focal fact; construction additionally requires incoming-focal and center mappings. Refraction underlies TIR. These concept dependencies do not duplicate complete tasks or disclose complete answer sets.
package_review.nonblocking_capacity_note: Recognition cannot establish unaided explanation, formula production or construction. Converging-only construction and focal supporting-line availability are explicitly bounded; no full-case construction approval is implied.
